newsitem.title: UK: NWE cracked fuel softer, weaker crude stalls deman.
newsitem.headline: NWE cracked fuel softer, weaker crude stalls deman.

text.p: NWE high sulphur cracked fuel oil prices ended softer on Monday as crude futures retraced early gains, and early refinery barge short-covering petered out, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded up to $101 a tonne fob ARA in early business with Shell still buying after refinery problems saw it an active player last week.
However, though the market was offered over this level in late business, easier crude continued to fuel bearish sentiment and buyers backed away. Barges traded at $98 up to $101 a tonne.
High sulphur cargo prices were slightly softer.

Sellers held offers around $98 a tonne cif NWE but trade remained thin with buyers some $3 a tonne lower. Some interest was seen for Russian E4 barrels at around three means +$2 a tonne but here too trade was thin and good avails were seen capping gains.

Low sulphur fuel oil dipped from early $1 gains to stand $1 down at $110 on the bid and unchanged at $114 a tonne cif NWE on the offer. Traders said there was little sign of fresh buying but sellers were reluctant to sell the market down.
Talk of poor refining margins and refinery run cuts stirred interest for straight run as a feed-stock.
